Lets say I go to a website and the cookie question pops up. Now I have 3 options: 1 accept. 2 leave the website. 3 stay and ignore (if possible) Since the question allways states thet either accepting the pop-up or using the website means you AGREE! I figure in all 3 cases the cookies have been placed, simply because I was foolish enough te ever enter the website. Anyone care to explain how it works and tell me I'm right or wrong?
When does a website start placing cookies?
Depends. Technically it can be done at any point; legally it should ask before it sets.

There's many different kinds of cookies in place:

  • Session cookies and such appear automatically and disappear when you close the browser. You can see them work when you close a tab and then open a new tab with the same site and magically get to the place you just left. They are always there and not much of a problem.

  • Local cookies can have different expiration dates, and remember that you visited the site. Useful for remembering settings w/o having to log in, but also to track you - whether you are a regular or not. Also allows collecting other data about you, like whether your IP address is fixed, and such. If you disagree, they might already be set, but should be deleted, and should not be used for analysis.

  • Third party cookies are the actual issue here. Put a little page element from a third party into your page, and it can not only store it's cookies, but also allow your page to gather third party info, and the third party to gather info from your servers - as much as both sides allow. Especially after scripting across different domains was made difficult, no-one saw a big problem here. But now we know that those cookies allow any web page you visit to get not just your ip address and with that your rough location, but also your name as on other social networks, your browsing habits as sold by your favourite search engine, and more. And they get either money or data in return. Usually both. Even more interesting is the fact that this works even if you don't have an account on a social network - because they will still profile you through ip addresses, browser settings, and other information, which leaves a very clear finger print of each of us.

In principle, all this is also possible by writing according code on the servers you connect to. But it would rely on the cooperation of the server admins, and that would be very difficult to enforce.
